title: A coal ship runs down a Ceann leathan boat
summary: A coal ship of A' Chompanaidh coming out of the river mouth on the ebb runs down a fishing boat of Ceann leathan off the bar and does not stop. The two men aboard are taken from the water alive by their neighbours. Within a season the town's boats keep inshore of the ships' track and lie to at the bar when a hull comes down.

title: Enoch Pratt offers Raghnall the staff
summary: In an Cèitean Enoch Pratt, agent of A' Chompanaidh at the pits of Muileann chrom, offers Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a staff of ash capped with brass, a weekly wage in marks and a house, to be set over all the crews of the hill and answer for them to the agent. Raghnall, forty-six years old, takes it.

title: Raghnall's slate-roofed house
summary: A' Chompanaidh's masons from Ros dhomhain build Raghnall mac Dhòmhnaill a house of two rooms and a loft on common grazing above the mill at Muileann chrom, with glass windows and a roof of slate, the first slate roof in the town. The miller's wife names him Raghnall Maor as he goes by, and the crews take up the name.

title: The roll of Taigh na Fèithe stops naming the overseers
summary: Marsaili nic Sheumais, who keeps the roll of Taigh na Fèithe, enters the first four overseers of the hill by name, then puts the matter to the custodians of the vein. From then on the roll gives only their number under the date, seven in the first year, and says of them only that several are hawk-faithful.

title: Seumas Dubh set over the pits at Cnoc mhòr
summary: When A' Chompanaidh opens new pits at Cnoc mhòr and asks for an overseer, Raghnall Maor gives the name of Seumas Dubh, who came into his crews at fifteen. Seumas takes the staff and goes south with his household to a crew of Cnoc mhòr men new to the seam, and runs the haulage three tubs to the rope.

title: Coinneach Beag crushed on the haulage
summary: The haulage rope at Cnoc mhòr parts under three full tubs, and the tubs run back into the gallery-mouth and crush Coinneach Beag, a boy of eleven coming up the rails with an empty. The custodians' roll of Cnoc mhòr gives his name, his age and his mother's name; A' Chompanaidh's report gives the cost of the rope.

title: The overseers made to stand at the hanging
summary: By Henry Maddox's order every overseer of the island stands in a row in front of the crowd at the hanging at Ros dhomhain, fourteen men with their staffs, inside a square of the soldiers of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach. The custodians' roll of Ros dhomhain enters in a line of its own that the overseers stood in front.

title: The two hanged named in the custodians' roll
summary: The roll of Cnoc mhòr names the two hewers hanged at Ros dhomhain for the killing of Seumas Dubh, Eòin Ruadh and Fionnlagh mac Aonghais, and records that their neighbours carried them home and buried them in the town's ground. The letter-book of Taigh an Àrd-mhaoir gives them as two of the crew.

title: A staff left at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr
summary: Riding home from the hanging, an overseer of Àth ìseal leaves his staff against the wall of Seònaid Bhàn's house at the half-way stage of Rathad na Mèinne, and in the morning it is gone. He tells the agent it is lost, and A' Chompanaidh gives him another.

title: The sermon in the road at Àth ìseal
summary: Turned back at the gate of the camp at Àth ìseal under Maddox's order by the hawk-faithful overseer Iomhar Bàn, an old priest of Òrd an t-Seabhaig sits down in the road outside the fence, and the crews come out to hear him there. When he is done Iomhar kneels in the road for his blessing. Raghnall Maor stands by.

title: The pox dead of the hill buried below Achadh dhomhain
summary: A' Bhreac Bhallach comes up Rathad na Mèinne into the camps of the hill in the last days of an Dàmhair, worst at Àth ìseal and Achadh dhomhain. A' Chompanaidh keeps the pits working. The custodians will not let the pox dead lie among the old graves, and the crews bury them by lamplight in new ground below Achadh dhomhain.

title: The custodians write their dead into the chaplains' margin
summary: Marsaili nic Sheumais goes from hearth to hearth on the hill in the spring and writes down the pox dead the chaplains had not found. The custodians borrow the chaplains' list, write their own names down both margins in the old letters with the total at the foot, and send it back to Ros dhomhain, where it is filed.

title: Beathag Dhubh dies at Doire mhòr
summary: Beathag Dhubh, custodian of Doire mhòr, who sent A' Chompanaidh's agent down the hill, dies in her own house in an Giblean at sixty-one, among the few hearths left lit after the stream was taken. She is laid out with Doire mhòr's own coal at her head and feet, and the whole hill comes up to her.

title: The hill buries Beathag Dhubh
summary: Some hundreds come up to Doire mhòr for Beathag Dhubh's burying, crews from the galleries unwashed among them, leaving A' Chompanaidh's cart-road at the bend to cross her fields by the old path. Raghnall Maor comes without his staff and stands at the back. The roll of Taigh na Fèithe writes her the last door of Doire mhòr that did not open.

title: Maddox's goods carried down to the ships
summary: For a week A' Chompanaidh's carts go down Rathad na Mèinne to Ros dhomhain with Henry Maddox's goods, a tall clock lashed upright in a cart of its own among them, and all go aboard the ship that brought Arthur Lisle. The carters say that he came out with one chest.

title: Lisle's rider gathers the papers of the hill
summary: Under Arthur Lisle's first order a rider of Riaghaltas nan Coigreach takes the papers of the pits at Muileann chrom down to Ros dhomhain: the contract of the first thirty and the paper of Raghnall's leader's share. Asked for the agreement that gave the overseers their staffs, Enoch Pratt finds that there is none.
